newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to higher Thursday, with blue chip shares clawing back some ground from yesterday's profit-taking as a strong technology sector moved the market higher.

While the Dow, which skidded lower Wednesday, might see some more selling pressure at the opening bell, strength in large-capitalization technology stocks following above-forecast results from Compaq Computer Corp would ultimately provide upward momentum, analysts said.

"Right now, we look like we're heading for a mixed open, with the market watching initial claims and retail sales," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. "But tech stocks will probably lead the market higher."

Shares of large technology companies would be lifted after Compaq reported better-than-expected second quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, excluding a $0.73 per share charge, analysts said. The First Call mean estimate was $1.39 per share. On a diluted basis, Compaq earned $0.75 per share.
"Compaq surprised on the upside, which might continue to light a fire underneath the technology sector," Cardillo said.
The Nasdaq composite, heavily-weighted with technology stocks, bucked Wednesday's declines by the Dow industrials to finish up 1.53 points at a record 1486.63.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, nervous as it hovered below the 8,000 level, shed 119.88 points at 7842.43.

"There is still a lot of interest in those large-capitalization technology companies which have been lagging, like Motorola Inc and Hewlett-Packard," Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said. "IBM is still strong, so large-cap techs should do well again today."
Brown said he expected the stock market to stabilize today after some early profit-taking, given strength in both the technology and bond markets.

Weaker-than-expected fourth quarter results from Seagate Technology Inc would not weigh much on the overall market because the computer disk drive maker had already warned investors about its results, he said.
Seagate reported $0.61 per share, excluding charges, versus $0.52 per share a year earlier, without charges.
The only economic data due out today were initial jobless clains for the week ended July 5.
They rose to 377,000 from 337,000 in the previous week, compared to a forecast 341,000 claims.
In early trade, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 0.02 points at a 6.57 percent yield, while the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off one point at 917.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 57.61 points, or 0.29 percent, at 19,754.78.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 4.1 at 4758.3.
U.S. stocks eased in London trading, weighed down by the technology sector.

In Europe, the dollar slipped to session lows against the mark, after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the dollar's correction against the mark was over. In Europe, the dollar was trading at 1.7548/57 marks and in Tokyo, the dollar traded at 112.62/72 marks.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that Wayne Huizenga, founder of WMX Technologies Inc, has lost some of his appeal on Wall Street.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that Disney Co's latest animated feature "Hercules" has had a poor showing compared with other Disney summer releases.
